record.original_question: Let F be a possibly singular foliation by Riemann surfaces on a compact Kähler manifold M, let T be an extremal positive ddc-closed current directed by F that gives full mass to the hyperbolic leaves, and for a universal covering map φ_a: D → L of a leaf define the Nevanlinna current τ_r^a. If Theorem 2.1 proves that τ_r^a converges to T for T-almost every a when all singularities of F are linearizable, does the same convergence still hold when the singularities are non-linearizable?

evidence.quote: Theorem 2.1 ([10]). In the above situation, assume that all singularities of F are linearizable. Then, for T-almost every a, we have τar → T as r tends to 1, in the sense of currents.
Problem 2.2. (i) Is Theorem 2.1 still true with non-linearizable singularities ? The question here is to estimate the Poincaré metric on leaves near a non-linearizable singularity.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a compact Kähler manifold and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a (possibly singular) holomorphic foliation by Riemann surfaces on $M$, with singular set $E$ consisting of isolated points. A singularity $p\in E$ is said to be linearizable if, in suitable local holomorphic coordinates centered at $p$, the foliation is defined by a linear vector field whose linear part is diagonalizable; otherwise $p$ is called non-linearizable.

Let $T$ be an extremal positive $dd^c$-closed current on $M$ directed by $\mathcal{F}$ (i.e., $T\wedge \omega = 0$ for any $(1,0)$-form $\omega$ vanishing on the tangent bundle of $\mathcal{F}$ on $M\setminus E$), and assume that $T$ gives full mass to the union of hyperbolic leaves of $\mathcal{F}$. For a point $a$ on a hyperbolic leaf $L_a$, fix a universal covering map $\varphi_a:\mathbb{D}\to L_a$ with $\varphi_a(0)=a$, where $\mathbb{D}$ is the unit disc. For $0<r<1$, define the Nevanlinna current
$$\tau_r^a \;=\; \frac{1}{T_r(a)}\,(\varphi_a)_*\!\Big(\log\tfrac{r}{|\zeta|}\,[\mathbb{D}_r]\Big),$$
where $\mathbb{D}_r=\{|\zeta|<r\}$ and $T_r(a)$ is the area-type normalization that makes $\tau_r^a$ a probability current.

It is known that, when all singularities of $\mathcal{F}$ are linearizable, one has $\tau_r^a \to T$ as $r\to 1$ in the sense of currents, for $T$-almost every $a\in M$.

Question: Does the same convergence $\tau_r^a\to T$ for $T$-almost every $a$ continue to hold when $\mathcal{F}$ is allowed to have non-linearizable singularities?
artifact.status_search_result: Web search shows the question is posed as an open problem requiring estimates of the Poincaré metric on leaves near non-linearizable singularities. Subsequent works (e.g., Dinh-Nguyen-Sibony's unique ergodicity results on compact Kähler surfaces, arXiv:1811.07450) treat related ergodic problems but do not appear to resolve the geometric Nevanlinna-current convergence in the non-linearizable case in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Unique Ergodicity for foliations on compact Kähler surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Unique ergodicity results for foliations with hyperbolic singularities; non-linearizable case not fully addressed.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work develops ergodic theorems but does not establish the geometric convergence of Nevanlinna currents at non-linearizable singularities in general.

status_evidence.title: Riemann surface foliations with non-discrete singular set
status_evidence.snippet: Recent paper on foliations with singularities, indicating active research on the subject.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues on foliations with various singularity types.
